titleEn: Poly B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver: Costs, Risks and What Homeowners Need to Know in 2026
titleZh: 温哥华Poly B管道更换：2026年费用、风险与须知
contentEn:
Poly B pipes — polybutylene pipes, manufactured from 1970 to 1995 — were installed in an estimated 700,000 homes across Canada. In Vancouver and the Lower Mainland, neighbourhoods built or renovated during that era still carry these pipes, and they are approaching or past their intended lifespan. If you own a home built before 1996 in Richmond, Burnaby, Surrey, or North Vancouver, understanding Poly B risk is essential before a small leak becomes a major insurance claim.

Plumbing experts and insurance assessors generally agree: Poly B pipes fail without warning. A pinhole leak can develop overnight, and a burst fitting can release thousands of litres of water in hours. This guide covers what the pipes look like, how to identify them, what replacement costs in 2026, and why acting before you sell protects both your home value and your family safety.

What Are Poly B Pipes and Why Are They a Problem?

Polybutylene (Poly B) pipes are grey or white plastic tubing, typically 1/2 inch to 1 inch in diameter, used for main water supply lines and branch runs in homes built between 1978 and 1995. They were chosen for their low material cost and ease of installation — a plumber could run an entire home water supply in hours rather than days.

The pipes degrade when exposed to chlorine and other drinking-water disinfectants that became standard in municipal supplies in the 1990s. Over 15 to 25 years, the pipe walls become brittle and micro-cracks develop. Fittings — especially elbow joints and coupling nuts — are the most common failure points, though any joint in the system can fail.

There is no reliable way to predict when a specific home Poly B system will fail. Some homes have experienced catastrophic failure within 12 years of installation; others have gone 30 years with only minor leaks. What insurers and plumbers agree on is this: when failure happens, it tends to be sudden and severe.

How to Identify Poly B Pipes in Your Home

The first step is visual identification. Poly B pipes have distinctive characteristics recognisable without special tools.

Colour and Markings

Authentic Poly B pipes are grey (sometimes appearing blue-grey) or off-white, with the printing POLYBUTYLENE 1/2INCH or PB 2110 stamped along the outer wall at regular intervals. Do not confuse grey Poly B with PVC — PVC is generally rigid and white or dark grey, while Poly B has some flexibility and a slightly waxy feel.

Locations to Check

  • Main water entry: Where the municipal supply enters the home, usually near the water meter or hot-water tank.
  • Basement ceiling: In unfinished basements, supply lines running horizontally are often visible.
  • Under sinks: The pipes feeding kitchen and bathroom sinks are frequently Poly B.
  • Behind toilets: The supply line to the toilet tank is a common Poly B location.
  • Around the hot-water tank: Both inlet and outlet connections are often Poly B.

Poly B Pipe Replacement Costs in Vancouver, 2026

Full repiping involves removing all Poly B piping and replacing it with copper or PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) piping. The cost varies based on the size of the home, the configuration of the existing plumbing, and whether walls need to be opened.

Home SizeEstimated Cost (2026 CAD)Typical Timeline
Condo / Townhouse (under 1,200 sq ft)3,500 - 7,0001 - 3 days
Single-Family Home (1,200 - 2,500 sq ft)8,000 - 18,0003 - 7 days
Large / Heritage Home (2,500+ sq ft)18,000 - 35,000+7 - 14 days

These estimates reflect material and labour costs in the Vancouver Metro area as of early 2026. PEX piping has become the preferred replacement material for most homeowners — it is flexible, freeze-resistant, and typically 20-30% less expensive than copper repiping. Copper remains the choice where durability and a long service life are the primary concerns.

Key cost factors include whether the home has concrete slab foundations (which can significantly increase opening costs), whether the electrical system must be temporarily relocated, and whether the municipality requires a permit for repiping (most do — a permit typically costs 200-500 and is included in a reputable plumber quote).

Does Home Insurance Cover Poly B Pipe Replacement?

Most standard home insurance policies in British Columbia cover sudden and accidental water damage — meaning if a Poly B pipe bursts and damages your floors, walls, or belongings, the damage repair may be covered. However, the cost of replacing the pipe itself is generally not covered, because it is considered a maintenance issue rather than a sudden event.

Some insurers have specific Poly B clauses or exclusions for homes with a known Poly B installation history. If you are purchasing a home built between 1978 and 1995, ask your insurance broker about the carrier position on Poly B before finalising the purchase.

How Long Does Poly B Pipe Replacement Take?

For a typical single-family home in the Vancouver area, the repiping process follows this general timeline:

  • Day 1: Plumber isolates the water supply, drains the system, and begins removing old Poly B piping.
  • Days 2-4: New PEX or copper piping is installed, including all connections to fixtures, the hot-water tank, and the municipal supply entry.
  • Day 5-6: System is pressure-tested to verify no leaks, then the water supply is restored.
  • Days 6-7: Wall patching, painting, and cosmetic repair.

Should You Replace Poly B Before Selling Your Vancouver Home?

Whether to replace Poly B before selling depends on your specific market and timeline. In Vancouver Lower Mainland, where homes regularly sell for 1M-3M+, a certified repipe is often a net positive. The cost of repiping (8,000-18,000 for a typical single-family home) is typically far less than the price reduction a buyer will demand if Poly B is disclosed.

If your home inspection identifies active leaks, wall staining, or corrosion at fittings, replacement is strongly advisable before listing. In a competitive offer situation, undisclosed Poly B can become a deal-killer discovered during the home inspection period.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my home has Poly B pipes?

Look for grey or white plastic pipes with POLYBUTYLENE or PB 2110 printed along the exterior. Common locations include the basement ceiling, under kitchen and bathroom sinks, near the hot-water tank, and at the main water entry point. A licensed plumber can confirm on a visual inspection in under an hour.

Is Poly B pipe replacement covered by home insurance in BC?

Water damage caused by a sudden Poly B pipe burst is typically covered under standard home insurance in British Columbia. The cost to replace the pipe itself is considered a maintenance expense and is generally not covered. Check with your insurer for any specific Poly B policy exclusions.

How much does it cost to replace Poly B pipes in Vancouver in 2026?

As of 2026, full Poly B replacement in the Vancouver Metro area typically ranges from 3,500-7,000 for a condo or townhouse, 8,000-18,000 for a typical single-family home, and 18,000-35,000+ for large or heritage homes. PEX piping costs 20-30% less than copper.

Should I replace Poly B pipes before selling my home?

Replacing Poly B before selling eliminates a significant negotiation point and can protect your sale price. In Vancouver competitive market, the cost of repiping is typically less than the discount an informed buyer will demand for the remediation risk.

Poly B管道（聚丁烯管道）于1970年至1995年期间生产，安装在约70万套加拿大住宅中。在温哥华和低陆平原地区，那个时代建造或翻新的房屋仍使用这些管道，且已接近或超过其预期使用寿命。如果您拥有1996年之前建成的列治文、本拿比、素里或北温房屋，了解Poly B风险至关重要——小渗漏可能在一夜之间变成重大保险索赔。

水管专家和保险评估员普遍认为：Poly B管道会在毫无预兆的情况下破裂。微孔渗漏可能一夜之间发生，而接头爆裂可能在数小时内释放数千升水。本指南涵盖管道的外观、识别方法、2026年更换费用，以及为何在出售前采取行动能保护您的房产价值与家人安全。

什么是Poly B管道？为什么是个问题？

聚丁烯（Poly B）管道是一种灰色或白色塑料管，直径通常为1/2至1英寸，用于1978年至1995年间建造房屋的供水主管和分支管道。20世纪90年代市政供水开始使用氯消毒剂后，塑料会降解。在15至25年内，管道壁变脆并产生微裂纹。接头（尤其是弯头和连接螺母）是最常见的故障点。

没有可靠的方法来预测特定房屋的Poly B系统何时会发生故障。有些房屋在安装后12年内就发生了灾难性故障；有些则30年来只有轻微渗漏。一旦发生故障，通常是突然且严重的。

如何识别家中的Poly B管道

Poly B管道具有独特的视觉特征。正宗Poly B管道为灰色（有时呈蓝灰色）或灰白色，外壁上印有POLYBUTYLENE 1/2INCH或PB 2110字样。不要将灰色Poly B与PVC混淆——PVC通常是硬质白色或深灰色，而Poly B有一定柔韧性。

常见检查位置包括：主进水口、地下室天花板、厨房和浴室水槽下方，马桶水箱供水管道，以及热水器进出水口连接处。

温哥华Poly B管道更换费用，2026年

全屋重铺管道涉及拆除所有Poly B管道并用铜或PEX管道替换。费用因房屋大小和是否需要开墙而异。

房屋类型预估费用（2026年加元）典型工期
公寓/联排（不足1,200平方英尺）3,500 - 7,0001 - 3天
独立屋（1,200 - 2,500平方英尺）8,000 - 18,0003 - 7天
大型/传统房屋（2,500+平方英尺）18,000 - 35,000+7 - 14天

PEX管道已成为大多数业主的首选替换材料——它具有柔性、抗冻且通常比铜管重铺便宜20-30%。

房屋保险是否承保Poly B管道更换？

卑诗省大多数标准房屋保险单承保意外水损——即如果Poly B管道爆裂并损坏您的地板、墙壁或物品，维修费用可能获得赔付。但更换管道本身的费用通常不在承保范围内，因为这被视为维护问题而非意外事件。

如果您正在购买1978年至1995年间建成的房屋，请在签约前向保险经纪询问保险公司对Poly B的立场。

规划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业翻新？获取Reno Stars的免费、无义务报价。

Poly B管道更换需要多长时间？

对于温哥华地区的典型独立屋，重铺管道过程大致为：第1天拆除旧管道；第2-4天安装新管道；第5-6天进行压力测试；第6-7天完成墙壁修补和装修。

常见问题

如何知道我的房屋是否有Poly B管道？

寻找带有POLYBUTYLENE或PB 2110印刷的灰色或白色塑料管道。常见位置包括地下室天花板、厨房和浴室水槽下方、热水器附近以及主进水口。许可水管工可在不到一小时内通过目视检查确认。

卑诗省房屋保险是否承保Poly B管道更换？

卑诗省标准房屋保险通常承保因意外Poly B管道爆裂造成的水损。更换管道本身的费用被视为维护费用，通常不在承保范围内。请向您的保险公司查询任何具体的Poly B保单排除条款。

2026年温哥华更换Poly B管道费用是多少？

截至2026年，温哥华都会区全面更换Poly B的典型费用为：公寓或联排别墅3,500至7,000；典型独立屋8,000至18,000；大型或传统住宅18,000至35,000以上。PEX管道是最常见的替换材料，成本比铜管低20%至30%。
